title: Boson Sampling Using Fock States from On-Demand Single Photon Source Arrays: Quantum Complexity & Impact of Dephasing
abstract: Boson sampling with array of on-demand single photons (discreet variable Fock states) as resource states provides distinct advantages in complexity scaling compared to single photon resource states mimicked by the states (continuous variable) generated in nonlinear photonics. Recent progress in realization of regular ordered array of mesa top single quantum dots (MTSQDs) enabling on-demand generation of many photon resource states with high single photon purity and indistinguishability [1,2] has opened the possibility of implementing chip-scale Boson sampling with single photons. An important question towards scale up of such circuits is how the dephasing and decay timescale of individual on-demand single photons affect the final probability distribution of the N-photon entangled state. In this work we report a framework that provides direct link between the physical sources of decoherence to the outcome of multiphoton correlation measurements. We explicitly incorporate the symmetrization of the N-photon states while accounting for the shape of the individual wave packets and dephasing. Using this framework, we show predictive estimates of the probability of generation of a 4-photon NOON state using an optical circuit initialized with 4 identical single photon wave packets, mimicking the emitted photons from MTSQD single photon sources reported in [2]. Specifically, we show how the probability of generating various 4-photon entangled states depend on the two-photon interference visibility which is determined by the pure dephasing timescale in relation to the radiative decay timescale. The results provide quantitative guidelines to measure 4 photon and higher number of entangled photon states generated in an optical circuit with on demand single photon sources and provide a link between physical processes such as temperature and the output state of the quantum optical circuits.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to calculate the performance of Boson Sampling using single photons from on-demand sources, explicitly accounting for decoherence effects like dephasing. By modeling the evolution of multi-photon wave packets, the authors show how physical parameters dictate the achievable probability of generating highly entangled states, offering vital guidelines for experimental quantum optics.
main_problem: The paper analyzes how decoherence (dephasing and decay) affects the probability distribution of N-photon entangled states generated via Boson Sampling using on-demand single photon sources.
main_result: The probability of generating entangled states, such as the 4-photon NOON state, depends quantitatively on the two-photon interference visibility, providing guidelines to link physical processes like temperature to quantum circuit output.
method: A theoretical framework is developed that links physical decoherence sources to multiphoton correlation measurements by explicitly incorporating state symmetrization and wave packet evolution.
model_or_system: The system models Boson Sampling using Fock states generated from arrays of on-demand single photon sources, specifically referencing Mesa Top Single Quantum Dots (MTSQDs). The theory tracks the evolution of the multi-photon wave packet through linear optical circuits.
key_observables: Probability of generating N-photon entangled states (e.g., NOON state), 2-photon coincidence count histogram, and the two-photon interference visibility ($V_{TPI}$).
important_parameters: Radiative decay lifetime ($T_1$), pure dephasing rate ($\gamma_{\phi}$), and the wave packet shape parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a weak-coupling limit for photonic devices and models the state evolution by transferring the symmetrization burden to the time-domain wave packet function.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MTSQD array enabling Fock state sampling, the single/multi-photon wave packet representations, and plots showing the dependence of $P_{NOON}$ and coincidence histograms on the dephasing rate ($T_2^*$).
paper_structure: The paper builds from describing the physical platform (MTSQDs) to developing a mathematical framework for multi-photon wave packet evolution, applying this framework to calculate specific observables like the 4-photon NOON state probability, and finally analyzing the dependence on decoherence timescales.
why_interesting: It provides a crucial quantitative link between fundamental physical noise processes (like dephasing) occurring at the single-photon source level and the measurable quantum complexity of a photonic quantum computation.
